narrative.overview:
The pass is the counter between the kitchen and the dining room, where every plate is checked before it goes out. The site is laid out like one: a clean, lit counter (the warm-paper ground) with the work set down on it to be inspected. The work is the product itself, shown in its own screenshots, its own stage names, its own documentation and, on the homepage, its own board drawn in code and running a simulated queue, and the site's job is to present it plainly enough that a lead can check it and sign off.

The system is the same one the board app uses, so the site and the product read as one object. It is flat and border-defined: surfaces are white panels with a 1px warm-grey edge, nothing is raised by a shadow, and a single enamel blue marks what can be acted on. Density is that of good documentation: generous line height, a 640–780px reading measure, and headings that state a claim on their own rather than waiting under a label. Light and dark are both first-class; the dark palette is a chosen set of warm near-blacks, not an inversion.

The kitchen appears in the words and the mark (a pleated toque) and may appear visually only in sparing, restrained nods that earn their place. The site must never become a dark hacker hero: no black-first terminal aesthetic, no neon, no animated code.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, white bordered surfaces, no shadows.
One accent, enamel blue, for actions, links, the mark and the current page.
Figtree for everything readable, JetBrains Mono for keys, paths and code.
The product carries the visual weight: screenshots in light and dark pairs, and on the homepage the simulated board itself.
Quiet and exact: thin borders, flat fills, precise spacing.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Enamel blue is the only accent on the site's own surfaces. Status colour (amber, green, red) appears only inside the simulated board and in product screenshots, where it means what it means in the app.

rules.name: The Needs-You Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber appears only inside the simulated board, and only where a person is needed: a card's Needs-you strip and edge, its amber dot, the Needs-you pill. It never decorates a page, a heading or a call to action.

rules.name: The Heading Carries Itself Rule
rules.body: A section heading stands alone, with no eyebrow, kicker or category label above it, and says something a reader can check ("Nothing merges without a person"). The uppercase 11px label belongs to navigation, the docs-sidebar group titles and the breadcrumb, where it names a place rather than introducing a heading.

rules.name: The Flat Counter Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are separated by borders and tone, never by shadow or blur. If something needs to stand out, give it the accent, not height: a card being moved by the cursor turns its edge Enamel Blue instead of lifting.

dos: Do take every colour from the custom properties in `site/src/site.css` (and, for the board status colours, the homepage's own mirror of them), and keep them identical to the board app's tokens.
Do separate surfaces with a 1px Border and a tonal step; keep everything flat.
Do show the product with its own screenshots, always as a light and dark pair, framed like a card.
Do let a section heading carry itself: a sentence that says something, with nothing above it.
Do label the simulated board as a simulation, pause it off screen, and start it paused under reduced motion.
Do set keys, paths, commands and versions in JetBrains Mono.
Do design both themes at once; dark is a warm near-black palette, not an inversion.
Do keep any kitchen imagery to a sparing, restrained nod that earns its place; the toque mark is the anchor.
donts: Don't add shadows, glows or blur to lift a surface.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, and don't use amber, green or red outside the simulated board; amber always means a person is needed.
Don't put an eyebrow, kicker or uppercase category label above a heading; the uppercase label is for navigation.
Don't turn the site into a dark hacker hero: no black-first terminal aesthetic, no neon green, no animated code.
Don't use emoji or exclamation marks, in copy or as icons.
